title: A microcontroller‐based, low‐cost platform for continuous pCO2 measurements in lakes and reservoirs
content:
Abstract

Continuous measurements of dissolved pCO2 are needed to resolve diel and event-scale variability in inland waters, but available instruments are either expensive or poorly suited to extended unattended deployments. We describe and evaluate a low-cost, modular platform that couples a marble-type gas–water equilibrator with a SenseAir K30 nondispersive infrared sensor housed in a microcontroller-based control unit (dry box) with passive silica-gel drying, a diaphragm pump and an Arduino data logger. The control unit costs about USD 180 and the complete system, including equilibrator and water pump, about USD 230. During a humidity stress test with more than 90 mL of nebulized water over 3 h, relative humidity in the sensor chamber increased by only 1.5 percentage points. Calibration against a laser-based greenhouse gas analyzer over 400–1800 ppm showed a linear response (slope 0.934, R 2 = 0.999), and the system stabilized within 1 min after field-like concentration changes. Deployed at a subtropical reservoir in southern Brazil for 78 d in three campaigns, with servicing between campaigns, the platform delivered 99.9% data completeness and resolved daily pCO2 ranges of 188 ± 149 μatm (maximum 866 μatm), anti-phase coupling with dissolved oxygen and a ~ 900 μatm increase during a cold-front mixing event. The system requires monthly desiccant replacement and periodic (≤ 6 months) recalibration of the nondispersive infrared sensor. Its accuracy is adequate for the large pCO2 variability of inland waters but not for marine carbonate-system monitoring. Open hardware and firmware make the platform suitable for distributed, low-budget monitoring networks.
